title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 169
paragraphs: Thus the Corcyreans evaded the Greek request. But the Cretans, when the Greeks sent to try to obtain their help, did this: they joined together and sent men to consult the god at Delphi, asking whether it would be better for them to come to Greece's aid. The Pythia answered: “You fools, do you think those woes too few that Minos sent upon you in his wrath because of the help you gave to Menelaus? For whereas they did not join with you in avenging Minos's death at Camicus, you nevertheless joined with them in avenging the woman who was carried off from Sparta by a barbarian.” When the Cretans heard this answer reported, they refrained from giving aid.
